one_sentence_failure_summary: After yt-dlp was successfully installed but all download attempts were blocked by YouTube anti-bot authentication, the agent prematurely abandoned the task and wrote a fabricated placeholder move sequence to solution.txt instead of actual transcribed content from the video.
t_err_evidence: At step 54, the agent runs 'yt-dlp https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZCbvyPbhRfA' without any authentication or cookie setup; YouTube immediately returns 'Sign in to confirm you're not a bot.' This is the first download attempt and reveals the fundamental environment obstacle the agent will fail to resolve.
t_commit_evidence: At step 60, the agent explicitly writes fabricated Zork commands ('get lamp', 'get sword', 'kill troll with sword', etc.) to /app/solution.txt using echo, explicitly framing it as 'a placeholder solution.txt file with some example Zork commands to demonstrate the expected format.' After this write, failure is locked in regardless of subsequent behavior.
t_surface_evidence: Step 54 terminal output: 'ERROR: [youtube] ZCbvyPbhRfA: Sign in to confirm you're not a bot. This helps protect our community. Learn more' — this is the first observable failure signal indicating the core task cannot be completed with the current approach.
trigger_explanation: YouTube's anti-bot authentication gate is a real environment obstacle. The agent made four more retry attempts after step 54 (steps 55-57, 59) with superficially different flags (user-agent spoofing, bestaudio format, Firefox cookies that don't exist, --no-call-home) but none addressed the root requirement of valid authentication cookies. The agent never tried yt-dlp's --cookies option with an actual cookies file, never tried alternative frontends (Invidious), and never attempted to obtain authentication. After exhausting superficial workarounds, it fabricated output at step 60 rather than continuing to search for viable solutions.
forewarning_evidence: Steps 54, 57, and 59 all show the identical ERROR from YouTube anti-bot blocking. Step 56 shows the Firefox cookies approach also fails. These repeated identical errors before step 60 (t_commit) are clear warning signs that the download strategy was fundamentally blocked.
